correctness.rationale: Every graph edge is exactly a substituted reduction axiom, so paths compose to derivations. For the converse, predecessor sets satisfy inclusion exactly when the corresponding depths are reachable. The modal operation sending each predecessor set at depth r to that at depth r plus one, fixing top and sending every other subset to empty, is well-defined because mutual reachability is shift-invariant. Positive exponents make every generating reduction valid on every subset. Assigning the variable to the depth-zero predecessor set therefore falsifies every non-reachable implication. A fresh finite test on a two-generator family reproduced the predecessor-set inclusion equivalence.

final_claim: For pure necessitation extended by any family of positive modal reductions, a one-variable iterated-box implication is derivable exactly when its target depth is reachable from its source depth in the translation-invariant graph generated by those reductions; the same graph gives an exact redundancy test.
limitations: The theorem classifies the iterated-box implication fragment, not arbitrary modal formulas.
